meta.title: Products
meta.description: Twelve apps: CRM, Chat, Groups, Agents, Flow, Robots, Track, Link, Docs, Notes, Cal and Board. Open source for your server, or on zerosoft Cloud with a free plan and usage-based pricing.

hero.sub: For your company: CRM, support, AI agents, automations, robots, projects and links. For you: docs, notes, scheduling and a whiteboard. The core of each one is open source and runs on your server for $0.

cta.sub: Sign in with Google, create a workspace and start on the free plan. If you later prefer your own server, the code is on GitHub.

meta.title: Link: short links on your domain, with analytics
meta.description: Short links with custom domains, cookie-less analytics, QR codes, link-in-bio, Bitly import, an API and webhooks. An open-source Bitly alternative.

hero.sub: Shorten links on your own domain, download the QR code and see clicks by country, referrer and device. Bring your Bitly account with a token or a CSV.

f1.d: go.yourcompany.com/slug. Add the DNS record and verify it; on zerosoft Cloud HTTPS is automatic. Each domain has its own slugs, and you choose where the root goes.

f2.d: Clicks by day, referrer, country, device, browser and OS. 7, 30 or 90 days or all time, compared with the previous period. No cookies, no fingerprinting.

f3.d: Every link has a QR code in SVG or PNG. Change the destination and the printed code still works.

f4.d: Protect a link with a password, give it an expiry date or a click cap. Once it is reached, the link stops redirecting.

f5.d: Paste a Bitly API token to bring the whole account, or upload the CSV export. Back-halves stay. Verify your domain here first and old links keep working when you move the DNS.

f6.d: One page at zerosoft.ai/@you. Pick your links, put them in order and share it. Clicks are still counted.

f7.d: Tag links by campaign, client or channel. Build UTM URLs without a spreadsheet. Find anything in seconds.

f8.d: Create and measure links from your code with REST API v1. Get link.created and link.clicked as signed webhooks, with retries.

f9.d: Your links as CSV and each link’s click log as CSV. You can also read everything through the API.

compare.note: Bitly Core costs $35 a month: $420 a year. Plans with more links and users cost more. Link on your server costs $0.

f1.q: How do I bring my links from Bitly?
f1.a: Paste a Bitly API token to import the account, or upload the CSV Bitly exports (up to 2,000 links per run). Back-halves are kept. Verify your domain here before you move the DNS and the old links keep working.

f2.a: Only if you give them an expiry date or a click cap. QR codes point at the short link, so you can change the destination without reprinting them.

f3.q: What does it record for each click?
f3.a: Country, referrer, device, browser and operating system, without cookies. Each link’s click log can be filtered by country and exported to CSV.

f4.a: Yes. REST API v1 creates, lists, edits and deletes links and returns their stats. The link.created and link.clicked webhooks are signed with HMAC.

f5.q: What is missing compared with Dub?
f5.a: Lead and sale tracking per click, a partner program, official SDKs, an MCP server and a CLI, one-click DNS setup and link cloaking. Routing by country or device, A/B destinations, QR codes with logo and colors, folder permissions and bulk actions are already in Link.

cta.sub: Paste a URL, pick the alias and share it.

s1.d: One link, or up to 200 at once. Already on Bitly? Import your links through its API or a CSV.

s2.d: Pick the alias, use your own domain, add UTM tags, a QR code, a password, an expiry date or a click limit.

s3.d: Cookie-less analytics by day, referrer, country, device, browser and OS. Export to CSV or get a webhook on every click.

meta.title: Track: open-source issues, cycles and Gantt
meta.description: Issues with sub-issues, cycles, estimates and list, board, calendar and Gantt views. An open-source Linear alternative.

hero.sub: Issues with sub-issues, relations, priorities and estimates. Plan in cycles and follow the work as a list, board, calendar or Gantt chart.

f1.d: Board, list, calendar and Gantt over the same issues.

f2.d: Group issues into one- or two-week cycles to plan each sprint.

f3.d: Issues with dates show up on a timeline the whole team can read.

f4.d: Break work into sub-issues and mark blockers and duplicates.

f5.d: Mentions, assignments and updates in one place. Mark them read and move on.

f6.d: Custom statuses per project and priorities from low to urgent.

f7.d: Point issues so everyone knows how big the work is before it starts.

f8.d: Filter by status, priority, assignee or cycle. Save the view, open it tomorrow.

f9.d: Every change is logged on the issue. Comment, mention and attach files.

compare.note: Linear Standard costs $8 per user per month. A team of 10 pays $960 a year. Track on your server costs $0.

f1.a: Yes. Paste a Linear API key, or upload a CSV export from Linear or Jira, or connect a GitHub repository. You see a preview first; projects, statuses, cycles, milestones, labels and comments come along, and importing again does not duplicate issues.

f2.a: By project. Each project has its own statuses, members, cycles and saved views. Issues have a priority, estimate, assignee, dates, sub-issues and relations.

f3.q: Where do I see my work?
f3.a: In My tasks and in the inbox, which collects mentions, assignments and changes to your issues.

f4.q: Does it have an API or webhooks?
f4.a: Not yet. API v1 covers Link, CRM, Cal and Agents. Meanwhile, Flow can create issues when something happens in another app.

f5.a: It ships in the same container as the rest of the suite. Issues live in your SQLite file and attachments in the uploads volume.

cta.sub: Create a project, invite the team and add this week’s issues.

s1.d: Create a project with your own statuses and invite the team to the shared workspace.

s2.d: Issues with sub-issues, relations, priorities and estimates. Group them into cycles to plan each sprint.

s3.d: Follow progress on a list, board, calendar or Gantt timeline. Comments, activity and an inbox keep everyone in sync.

meta.title: CRM: open-source contacts, deals and pipelines
meta.description: Contacts, companies, pipelines, Gmail email sequences, forms, quotes and reports. An open-source HubSpot alternative that runs on your server.

hero.sub: Contacts, companies and deals on a kanban pipeline. It syncs Gmail, sends sequences, captures leads with forms and builds quotes. Your HubSpot export comes in with a preset.

f1.d: Drag deals between stages on a kanban board. As many pipelines as you need, with a probability per stage and a reason for every lost deal.

f2.d: Contacts, companies and deals linked to each other, with company hierarchies, tags, custom fields and duplicate detection.

f3.d: Connect Gmail and every email lands on the contact timeline. Sequences send several steps and stop when someone replies.

f4.d: Calls, meetings, notes and tasks on one timeline per record. Meetings booked in Cal show up on their own.

f5.d: Funnel, forecast, sources, quotas per rep and dashboards with widgets. Reports can be saved.

f6.d: Contacts, companies and deals from any CSV, with column mapping and a preset for the HubSpot export. Export to CSV or JSON.

f7.d: Embeddable forms that create the contact, assign it round-robin and score it with your rules.

f8.d: When a record is created or changes, an email arrives or a quote is accepted: create a task, send an email, call a webhook or enroll in a sequence.

f9.d: A REST API with per-key scopes for contacts, companies, deals, tasks, products and quotes. Signed webhooks when contacts and deals change.

compare.note: HubSpot Sales Hub Professional starts around $50 per user per month. Ten reps pay $6,000 a year before onboarding. CRM on your server costs $0.

f1.q: How do I bring my data from HubSpot?
f1.a: Connect HubSpot (or Pipedrive) with a read-only token in the importer: contacts, companies, deals, pipelines, owners, custom properties and the activity timeline come over, with a preview first and no duplicates if you run it again. You can also upload CSV exports with the «HubSpot export» preset.

f2.q: Does it send email from my account?
f2.a: Yes, from your connected Gmail, with templates, open and click tracking, and sequences. Sequence steps go out within the hour they are due. On your own server, connecting Gmail needs your own Google OAuth client.

f3.q: Can I limit what each rep sees?
f3.a: Yes. You choose whether members see every record, only their own, or their sales team’s. The rule also applies to search, reports, exports and the API.

f4.a: Yes. REST API v1 covers contacts, companies, deals, activities, tasks, pipelines, products, quotes, associations, tags and forms. Each key has scopes (crm:read, crm:write) and acts with the permissions of whoever created it.

f5.q: What is missing compared to HubSpot?
f5.a: Quotes have no e-signature or payment collection. Forms have no multi-step pages, conditional fields or file uploads. On phones, tables scroll sideways instead of switching to cards.

cta.title2: With the data you already have.
cta.sub: Import a CSV from HubSpot or a spreadsheet and start moving deals.

s1.d: Import contacts and companies from any CSV, mapping each column to a field, with duplicates detected for you.

s2.d: Move deals across the stages of one or several pipelines on a kanban board. Log calls, notes and tasks on each timeline.

s3.d: Workflows send emails, create tasks or call webhooks when something changes. Reports and dashboards show where the money is.

meta.title: Cal: booking pages with Google Calendar
meta.description: Booking pages synced with Google Calendar and Meet, round-robin, routing forms, embeds, an API and webhooks. An open-source Calendly alternative.

hero.sub: Share a link, the other person picks a time and the meeting lands in your Google Calendar with a Meet link. Reminders, rescheduling and cancellation included.

f1.d: One link per meeting: zerosoft.ai/book/you/30min. Days with nothing free are disabled. On desktop, calendar and slots side by side.

f2.d: Busy in Google means busy here. Every booking lands in your calendar, with a Google Meet link when there is no other location. Reschedule or cancel and it updates.

f3.d: Guests see their time zone and you see yours. Buffers before and after, minimum notice and custom questions.

f4.d: Ask a few questions, send each person to the right event type, spread bookings across the team. Each host connects their own Google Calendar.

f5.d: They cancel or reschedule from the link in the email, without creating an account.

f6.d: Confirmation, reschedule and cancellation emails carry an .ics invite. A reminder goes out 24 hours before, with the link to manage the booking.

f7.d: Inline on any page (the height adjusts itself) or behind a popup button.

f8.d: REST API v1 for event types and bookings: list, create, get, cancel. booking.created, booking.rescheduled and booking.cancelled as signed webhooks, with retries.

f9.d: Availability is per person across all your event types, so two guests cannot take the same slot. You can also block holidays or focus time.

compare.note: Calendly Standard costs about $12 per user per month. Ten people pay $1,440 a year. Cal on your server costs $0.

f1.q: How do I move over from Calendly?
f1.a: Paste a Calendly personal access token in Cal settings, under Import from Calendly. Event types (duration, locations and questions) and availability schedules come over, and upcoming bookings too if you choose. Then connect Google Calendar and replace the link or embed on your site.

f2.q: Which calendars does it sync with?
f2.a: Google Calendar: busy times block slots and every booking creates the event with a Meet link. Outlook and iCloud are not supported yet. On your own server, the Google connection needs your own OAuth client.

f3.q: Does it work for a team?
f3.a: Yes. An event type can have several hosts and assigns the booking round-robin to whoever is free. Routing forms send each person to the right event type.

f4.a: Yes. REST API v1 lists event types and creates, lists and cancels bookings with the same rules as the public page. The booking.created, booking.rescheduled and booking.cancelled webhooks are signed.

f5.q: What is missing compared to Calendly?
f5.a: Group or collective events, SMS reminders and Outlook or iCloud calendars. Stripe payments, email workflows and reusable schedules are already in Cal.

cta.sub: Create an event type, connect Google Calendar and send the link.

s1.d: Set the duration, the questions you need answered, your weekly availability, buffers and minimum notice.

s2.d: Send your booking link or embed it on your site, inline or as a popup. Round-robin spreads meetings across the team.

s3.d: The meeting lands in Google Calendar with a Meet link. Everyone gets the invite and a 24h reminder; guests can reschedule or cancel on their own.

meta.title: Docs: a wiki and documents with a block editor
meta.description: Nested pages, a block editor with a / menu, links between pages, mentions, comments and templates. An open-source Notion alternative.

hero.sub: A wiki for your team: nested pages, a block editor with a / menu, page links with [[, @mentions and comments on any block.

f1.d: Paragraphs, headings, lists, to-dos, quotes, code blocks and tables. Type '/' and keep writing.

f2.d: Organize pages in a tree and drag them to nest one under another.

f3.d: Type [[ to link another page and @ to mention someone in the workspace.

f4.d: Comment on the whole page or on one block. Threads can be resolved and reopened.

f5.d: Invite the whole company. Seats are not billed, on your server or on zerosoft Cloud.

f6.d: Every page is stored as JSON in your database. If you self-host, it sits in your SQLite file.

f7.d: Find pages from ⌘K, alongside contacts, links and tasks.

f8.d: Start from meeting notes, a project spec or a weekly retro.

f9.d: Moving a page to the trash takes its subpages with it, and restoring brings them all back.

compare.note: Notion Plus costs about $10 per user per month. A team of ten pays $1,200 a year. Docs on your server costs $0.

f1.a: Yes. Export your workspace or a page from Notion as Markdown & CSV and upload the .zip in Docs › Import from Notion. Pages keep their tree, images, files and links between pages; each CSV becomes a database, and each row's page becomes the body of that row.

f2.q: Can several people edit at once?
f2.a: Not in real time. If two people edit the same page at the same time, the second one to save gets a warning and chooses between loading the new version or overwriting it. Each page keeps up to 50 versions you can restore.

f3.q: Can I publish a page on the web?
f3.a: Yes. The pages you publish form a public help center at /h/ plus your handle, with collections, search and a vote per article. On zerosoft Cloud there is no custom domain yet. For a single person, share the page as view only.

f4.a: Typed properties (text, number, select, multi-select, status, date, person, checkbox, URL, email, phone, created and edited time), table, board and gallery views with filters, sorting and grouping, and rows that open as pages. Relations, rollups, formulas and calendar or timeline views are not there yet.

f5.q: Does it have a public API?
f5.a: Not yet. API v1 covers Link, CRM, Cal and Agents. If you self-host, pages are stored as JSON in your SQLite database.

cta.sub: Start from a template and nest pages as it grows.

s1.d: Start from a blank page or a template, and nest pages inside pages to build your wiki.

s2.d: Headings, lists, to-dos and more from the slash menu. Link other pages with [[ and leave comments.

s3.d: Leave comments on any block and find any page from ⌘K.

meta.title: Chat: website chat widget and shared inbox
meta.description: A chat widget for your site, a shared inbox, SLAs, assignment rules, canned responses, an AI bot and CSAT. An open-source Intercom alternative.

hero.sub: A chat widget for your site and a shared inbox for the team. Statuses and priorities, SLAs, assignment rules, canned responses, an AI bot and CSAT.

chat.featuresTitleDim: With the whole team in it.

f1.d: One script tag puts the widget on any site. If you identify the visitor, you see their name and email.

f2.d: Every conversation lands in one inbox the whole team works: assign, reply, snooze and resolve. J and K move between them.

f3.d: Open, pending, snoozed and resolved, with priorities from low to urgent.

f4.d: First-response and resolution targets per priority, with a warning before they are breached.

f5.d: Answers from your canned responses and Docs pages, and hands off to a person at high priority. Without AI configured, it matches by keyword.

f6.d: Show an away message with your expected response time when you're off, and measure satisfaction (1–5) when a conversation is resolved.

f7.d: Route conversations to the right teammate automatically and answer in two keystrokes with saved replies.

f8.d: Your visitors with their conversations and notes. If they leave an email, one click adds them to the CRM.

f9.d: Invite your whole support team. Seats are not billed.

compare.note: Intercom starts around $29 per seat per month. A team of ten pays $3,480 a year. Chat on your server costs $0.

f1.q: How do I add the widget to my site?
f1.a: Create a widget, copy the script tag and paste it before the closing body tag. It works on any site that serves HTML.

f2.q: Does it handle email or WhatsApp?
f2.a: Not yet. Chat has one channel: the website widget.

f3.a: It answers until someone on your team replies. It uses AI with your canned responses and Docs pages; without AI configured, it matches by keyword. You can turn it off per widget.

f4.q: Does it connect to the CRM?
f4.a: Yes. If the visitor leaves an email, Chat creates the contact in the CRM and logs the conversation on its timeline.

f5.q: What is missing compared to Intercom?
f5.a: Proactive messages, a public API with webhooks, and conversation export. Internal notes with mentions, tags, macros, the help center and reports per agent or by date range are already in Chat.

cta.sub: Create a widget, paste the script on your site and get your first message.

s1.d: Copy one script tag into your site. Visitors get a webchat that respects your office hours.

s2.d: Every conversation lands in a shared inbox, with states, priorities, assignment rules and SLA timers.

s3.d: Canned responses for the usual questions and an AI bot that handles the repeats. CSAT tells you how it went.

meta.title: Groups: open-source WhatsApp team inbox and group manager
meta.description: A shared inbox for WhatsApp chats and groups: assignment, notes, tickets by emoji, SLAs, broadcasts and bulk group management, linked to your CRM. An open-source Periskope alternative.

hero.sub: One inbox for every WhatsApp chat and customer group. Assign, answer, turn messages into tickets and manage hundreds of groups at once, with each group on its CRM record.

groups.featuresTitle: Every customer group in one place.

f1.d: 1:1 chats and groups from several numbers in one list, with filters for unread, unanswered, mine and label.

f2.d: Create groups one by one or from a CSV, add and remove members in many groups, promote admins and reset invite links.

f3.d: React with an emoji from the app or the phone, or use a keyword, and the message becomes a ticket with priority and due time.

f4.d: A chat that waits longer than your limit shows up as overdue. A reply from the phone also counts.

f5.d: One message with variables to many groups, now or scheduled, with messages per minute and status per recipient.

f6.d: Link a group to a company or contact and its latest messages and open tickets show up there.

f7.d: An agent from Agents can answer in a chat, and Flow reacts to messages and tickets or sends a WhatsApp.

f8.d: Use the WhatsApp Cloud API for 1:1 support, or a WAHA or Evolution API gateway by QR to manage groups.

f9.d: J and K to move, R to reply, N for a note, E to close, A to assign and T for a ticket.

compare.note: Periskope Starter lists at $25 per seat per month (monthly billing, Pro is $35). A team of ten pays $3,000 a year. Groups on your server costs $0; you run the WhatsApp gateway or pay Meta for the official API.

f1.q: How does it connect to WhatsApp?
f1.a: Two ways, chosen per number. The official WhatsApp Cloud API from Meta, for 1:1 chats, media and templates. Or a self-hosted WAHA or Evolution API gateway that links your number by QR, which is what allows group management.

f2.q: Is the QR mode safe for my number?
f2.a: It uses an unofficial WhatsApp Web session, and WhatsApp can restrict a number used this way, especially if it adds many strangers or sends a lot of unrequested messages. Groups sends broadcasts at a pace you set and suggests invite links. For 1:1 messaging we recommend the official API.

f3.q: Can I manage groups with the official API?
f3.a: Not in Groups today. The official API covers 1:1 chats; creating groups and managing members goes through the QR gateway.

f4.a: A ticket comes from a message: by hand, by reacting with the ticket emoji (from Groups or the phone) or when a customer writes one of your keywords. Each one has status, priority, assignee and due times for first response and resolution.

f5.q: What is missing compared to Periskope?
f5.a: Still to come: a native mobile app, voice calls, round-robin assignment and per-label access for members. Periskope also uses AI to tell questions from comments; Groups flags by time without reply.

cta.sub: Connect a number, bring in your groups and start answering from one inbox.

s1.d: Paste your Cloud API credentials or scan the QR from your gateway.

s2.d: Sync the groups the number already has, or create them from a CSV.

s3.d: Assign chats, leave notes, open tickets and link each group to the CRM.

meta.title: Agents: AI agents that use your knowledge
meta.description: AI agents that answer from your own knowledge and use tools across CRM, Cal, Track and Flow. An open-source alternative to Intercom Fin.

hero.sub: AI agents that help your customers using your own knowledge and act across the suite: they save leads, book meetings and hand off to your team when needed.

f1.d: Describe what it does, how it talks and when it uses each tool, the way you would brief a new hire.

f2.d: It searches your Docs pages, up to 20 URLs (each one is read as a single page; it does not crawl the site) and your saved Chat replies.

f3.d: It saves leads to the CRM, offers times and books in Cal, files Track issues and runs flows.

f4.d: When the visitor asks or the agent is unsure, it alerts your team and stops replying.

f5.d: Your site’s Chat widget, a full-screen public page and an API for your own app.

f6.d: Test it before you publish, and every conversation records which tools it used and with what data.

compare.note: Intercom charges about $0.99 for every conversation Fin resolves, on top of Intercom seats. At 1,000 resolutions a month that is $11,880 a year. Agents on your server costs whatever your AI model uses.

f1.q: Which AI model does it use?
f1.a: Any model on the AI Gateway, in provider/model format (for example, anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5). On your server you pay usage directly with your key; on zerosoft Cloud it is billed by tokens.

f2.a: It answers from your knowledge and hands off to a person when it is unsure. Every reply is logged with the tools it used, so you can review it.

f3.q: Where does it talk to my customers?
f3.a: In the Chat widget on your site, on its own public page and through API v1 (agents:run scope) from your app.

f4.a: Only through the tools you turn on, and only inside your workspace. To book a meeting it needs a slot it offered itself and the visitor’s confirmation.

f5.q: Can I bring my Fin setup?
f5.a: There is no importer. Paste your instructions as the brief and add your Docs pages and the URLs of your web pages as knowledge.

cta.sub: Create an agent from a template and try it in the playground before you publish it.

s1.d: Pick a template (support, sales or lead qualification) or start blank.

s2.d: Add Docs pages and websites, and turn on only the tools it needs.

s3.d: Connect it to the Chat widget, share its page or call it through the API.

meta.title: Flow: open-source visual automations
meta.description: Visual automations across every zerosoft app and any API. An open-source alternative to Zapier and n8n.

hero.sub: Visual automations across every zerosoft app and any service with an API. Triggers, conditions, loops and AI steps on one canvas.

f1.d: A Cal booking, a Link click, a new contact, an issue or a Chat message.

f2.d: Start from a POST to a secret URL or every N minutes, in your time zone.

f3.d: Conditions, branches and loops over lists, on a canvas where you drag and connect nodes.

f4.d: Create contacts, enroll in sequences, open issues, reply in Chat and write to Docs.

f5.d: Summarize, classify or draft text in the middle of a flow.

f6.d: Every run keeps what went in and out of each node, so you find the error fast.

compare.note: Zapier Team costs about $103.50 a month billed monthly and includes 2,000 tasks; go past that and the price goes up. Flow on your server does not charge per task.

f1.a: An event in any app (a booking, a click, a new contact, an issue, a chat message), an incoming webhook, a schedule or the Test button.

f2.q: Does it connect to outside services?
f2.a: Yes: through HTTP requests to any public HTTPS API and through incoming webhooks. To post in Slack, its webhook is enough.

f3.a: There is no importer. Templates cover the most common cases, and building a new flow takes minutes.

f4.a: On your server there is no per-task charge. Each workspace has an hourly run cap so a broken loop does not overload the server.

f5.q: What is missing compared to Zapier?
f5.a: The number of integrations. Flow has nodes for Slack, Google Sheets, Gmail, Stripe, Notion, Discord and Telegram; Zapier connects thousands of apps. For the rest, Flow speaks HTTP: if a service has an API or webhooks, you connect it with an HTTP request.

cta.sub: Start from a template and turn on your first flow today.

s1.d: An event in the suite, an incoming webhook or a schedule.

s2.d: Add conditions, loops, HTTP requests, emails and actions from each app.

s3.d: Run a test with real data, check each node’s output and switch it on.

meta.title: Robots: open-source browser automation
meta.description: Robots that browse, fill in forms and extract data for you. An open-source alternative to UiPath.

hero.sub: Browser robots that visit pages, click, fill in forms and extract data for you. Run them by hand, on a schedule or from Flow.

f1.d: Open a URL, click, fill in, wait, extract text or tables and take screenshots.

f2.d: Define named values and the same robot works for another product or another page.

f3.d: It walks through lists of items and decides what to do based on what it finds.

f4.d: It runs every day at the time you choose, or by hand when you need it.

f5.d: A flow starts it, waits for the result and uses the data in the next step.

f6.d: Each run opens a fresh browser and closes it when done. On Vercel, inside a microVM.

compare.note: UiPath Basic starts at about $25 a month for up to 2 robots; Standard and Enterprise are quoted separately. Robots on your server costs $0; on Vercel you pay for the Sandbox minutes you use.

f1.a: A browser that follows steps: open a page, click, fill in fields, read text or tables and take screenshots. You build it step by step, without writing code.

f2.a: On your server with Chromium, or in an isolated Vercel Sandbox microVM if you deploy on Vercel.

f3.q: Does it work on sites with a login?
f3.a: Yes. Store the username and password in Flow Credentials: they are encrypted with AES-256-GCM and the robot uses them without showing them in the logs. It can also keep the session between runs, encrypted. Regular inputs are stored in plain text and the whole workspace can see them, so do not put passwords there.

f4.q: How do I use what it extracts?
f4.a: Every run returns JSON. From Flow you can create contacts, send an email or file an issue with that data.

f5.q: What is missing compared with Browse AI?
f5.a: Picking what to extract by clicking on the page (today you write CSS selectors), prebuilt robots for popular sites, robots generated by AI from a URL, residential proxies by country, captcha handling and self-healing when a site changes its layout.

cta.sub: Start from a template: read a table, track a price, fill in a form or take a screenshot.

s1.d: Start with Go to URL and add clicks, fields and extractions.

s2.d: Run it by hand and see what it extracted at each step.

s3.d: Give it a schedule or call it from a flow.

meta.title: Notes: open-source notes, notebooks and search
meta.description: Notebooks, checklists, a web clipper and questions about your notes. An open-source alternative to Evernote.

hero.sub: Quick notes, notebooks, checklists and full-text search. Save pages with the clipper and ask your notes what you forgot.

f1.d: Organize your way and keep what you use every day at the top.

f2.d: Find a note by any word inside it.

f3.d: Lists to tick off, from groceries to opening the shop.

f4.d: Save any page as a note, with the text you selected and the source link.

f5.d: Answers that come only from your notes, with the sources in view.

f6.d: Share a note with anyone and switch the link off when you are done.

compare.note: Evernote Personal costs about $14.99 a month billed monthly. Notes on your server costs $0.

meta.title: API docs
meta.description: The zerosoft REST API for Link, CRM, Cal and Agents. Personal keys with scopes and JSON responses.

docs.label: API
docs.title: The zerosoft API.
docs.intro: Link, CRM, Cal and Agents expose a REST API with JSON responses and personal keys.
docs.authDesc: Every request needs an API key, sent as a Bearer token. For browser sessions the Google OAuth flow creates the session cookie.
docs.authNote: Create keys in Dashboard → Settings → API keys. A key is shown exactly once: copy it and store it like a password. Each key allows 100 requests per minute.
docs.linksDesc: Create, list, update and measure short links.
docs.authFlowDesc: Redirect the user to start the Google OAuth flow. After success they return to the app with a session cookie.
docs.linksCreateDesc: Creates a short link with the same options as the app: UTM, expiration, click limit, password, social preview, targeting and an externalId. slug is optional: leave it out and we generate one.
docs.linksListDesc: Your links, newest first. Paginate with page and pageSize (max 100).
docs.linksDeleteDesc: Delete a link by id, along with its click history. The person who created the API key must be a workspace admin.
docs.linksPatchDesc: Update any writable field of a link.
docs.linksStatsDesc: Click totals and a per-day breakdown for one link.
docs.linksAnalyticsDesc: Clicks and QR scans across all your links in a range: per day, top links, referrers, countries, devices and browsers. Up to 366 days.
docs.contactsListDesc: List contacts. Filters: q, page, pageSize (max 100).
docs.contactsPatchDesc: Update any property of a contact.
docs.companiesListDesc: List companies. Filters: q, page, pageSize.
docs.companiesPatchDesc: Update any property of a company.
docs.dealsCreateDesc: Create a deal in a pipeline stage.
docs.tasksListDesc: List tasks. bucket: overdue, today, upcoming, done.
docs.tasksCreateDesc: Create a task, optionally linked to a record.
docs.stagesCreateDesc: Create a stage inside a pipeline.
docs.teamsInviteDesc: Invite an email to join a team.
docs.teamsSwitchDesc: Switch active workspace. Use teamId: null for the personal workspace.
docs.docsPatchDesc: Update title, content or archive a page.
docs.paramLinkId: Link id, or ext_ followed by the externalId you set when creating it.
docs.paramFrom: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to 29 days ago.
docs.paramLinkTargeting: Country and device rules, weighted A/B destinations and iOS/Android deep links. null clears them.
docs.paramTaskBucket: Filter bucket: overdue, today, upcoming, done.
docs.paramTeamIdSwitch: Team id or null for the personal workspace.
docs.calDesc: Event types and bookings. Bookings created through the API follow the same rules as the public page (availability, buffers, Google Calendar busy times) and send the same emails.
docs.calEventTypesDesc: Your event types with their public booking URL.
docs.calBookingsListDesc: Bookings of your event types, newest first. Filter by status and date range.
docs.calBookingsCreateDesc: Books a slot for a guest. Returns 409 slot_unavailable if the time isn't offered anymore.
docs.calBookingsGetDesc: One booking by id (event type owner or assigned host).
docs.calBookingsCancelDesc: Cancels a confirmed booking, emails the guest a cancellation with .ics, removes the Google Calendar event and emits booking.cancelled.
docs.calBookingsRescheduleDesc: Moves a confirmed booking to another offered time, emails the guest the updated .ics and emits booking.rescheduled. Returns 409 slot_unavailable if that time is not offered.
docs.calBookingsNoShowDesc: Marks that the guest did not show up. Confirmed bookings only.
docs.agentsDesc: Talk to your AI agents from your own app. The agent uses the same instructions, knowledge and tools as in Chat and on its public page; every reply counts toward the workspace AI quota.
docs.agentsMessagesTitle: Send a message to an agent
docs.agentsMessagesDesc: Returns the agent's reply and the tools it used. Send the returned conversationId to continue the same conversation. Errors: 404 not_found, 403 agent_disabled, 429 rate_limited, 503 ai_disabled.
docs.robotsDesc: Run your browser robots from your own app, one at a time or over many inputs. Runs go through the same queue as in the app (one at a time per workspace) and count toward the monthly robot minutes. Running needs a key created by a workspace admin.
docs.robotsListDesc: Returns the workspace robots with their inputs, so you know what to send when running them.
docs.robotsRunDesc: Queues a run and returns 202 with the run; poll GET /api/v1/robots/runs/:id until status is success or failed. With "wait": true the response waits for the result (200) when no other run is ahead. The robot needs automatic runs turned on. Errors: 404 not_found, 400 missing_input or disabled, 409 busy, 429 rate_limited or quota_exceeded, 503 runner_unavailable.
docs.robotsRunGetDesc: Status, inputs and extracted data of a run. changed tells whether the data differs from the previous successful run with the same inputs (null when there was nothing to compare).
docs.robotsBulkTitle: Run a robot over many inputs
docs.robotsBulkDesc: Queues one run per item of inputs (up to 100) under a batch id. Runs start one after another; every input is validated before anything is queued. Errors: 400 missing_input (with the item index), 409 busy, 429 rate_limited.
docs.robotsBatchGetDesc: Counts by status, done when every run finished, and the input, output and error of each run in the order you sent them.
docs.paramAgentMessage: What the user says (up to 4000 characters).
docs.paramAgentConversationId: Continue an existing API conversation. Omit it to start a new one.
docs.paramRobotInputs: Robot inputs by name. List inputs take an array of strings.
docs.paramRobotWait: Wait for the result in the same response (up to the robot timeout). Default false.
docs.paramRobotBulkInputs: One inputs object per run, 1 to 100.
docs.webhooksDesc: Add endpoints in Dashboard → Settings → Webhooks. Events: booking.created, booking.rescheduled, booking.cancelled, booking.no_show, booking.requested, link.created, link.clicked, link.updated, link.deleted, contact.created, contact.updated, deal.created, deal.updated, deal.stage_changed, deal.won, deal.lost, robot.run.finished, robot.run.failed, robot.output.changed, chat.message.created, chat.conversation.assigned, chat.conversation.resolved. Link events can be limited to some links, tags or domains. link.updated carries the link and the list of changed fields; link.deleted, the link as it was. Each request carries Zerosoft-Signature: t=TIMESTAMP,v1=HEX, where v1 = HMAC-SHA256(secret, "TIMESTAMP.RAW_BODY"). Reject old timestamps. Failed deliveries are retried with backoff for ~15 hours.
docs.webhooksPayloadDesc: What your endpoint receives. Respond 2xx within 8 seconds.
docs.paramCalQuery: Searches the guest's name or email.
docs.paramCalEventTypeId: Event type id (from List event types).
docs.paramCalStart: Slot start, must match an offered slot.
docs.paramCalEmail: Guest email: receives the confirmation and calendar invite.
docs.paramCalTimezone: Guest timezone for the emails. Defaults to UTC.
docs.paramCalReason: Shown to the guest in the cancellation email.
docs.contactsDeleteDesc: Permanently deletes the contact. Its activities stay, unlinked.
docs.companiesDeleteDesc: Permanently deletes the company. Contacts keep existing without a company.
docs.dealsMoveTitle: Move a deal to a stage
docs.dealsMoveDesc: Moves the deal to another stage of its pipeline. Won/lost stages close it; a lost stage needs lostReason. If the stage requires properties the deal lacks, it answers 422 missing_required with the list; send them in fields to fill them in and move in one call. Fires deal.stage_changed (and deal.won / deal.lost).
docs.crmActivitiesDesc: The timeline of a contact, company or deal: notes, calls, meetings, emails and tasks. Meetings booked in Cal show up here automatically.
docs.activitiesListDesc: Most recent first. Pass exactly one of contactId, companyId or dealId.
docs.activitiesCreateDesc: Log a note, call, meeting or email on a record. Tasks have their own endpoint.
docs.paramContactIds: IDs of the contacts to enroll (1–500).
docs.paramLostReason: Why it was lost (required for lost stages).
docs.paramRecordFilter: The record whose timeline you want.
docs.paramActivityBody: Free text: notes, call summary, email body.
docs.crmEmailDesc: Shared email templates and snippets, and multi-step sales sequences. Sequence emails are sent from the sender's connected Gmail; steps run on the hourly scheduler.
docs.emailTemplatesListDesc: Templates and snippets shared in the workspace. Variables go between double curly braces (contact.first_name, contact.company, deal.name, owner.first_name, contact.custom.x), with an optional fallback after a pipe.
docs.sequencesListDesc: Sequences with their number of steps and enrollments.
docs.sequencesEnrollDesc: Enrolls up to 500 contacts. Contacts that are already enrolled, unsubscribed or without email are returned in skipped. The sender needs Gmail connected with send permission.
docs.sequencesUnenrollDesc: Removes the contact from the sequence (status exited, reason manual).
docs.paramTemplateKind: Filter by kind: template or snippet.
docs.paramSenderId: Workspace member whose Gmail sends the emails. Defaults to the contact owner, then the sequence creator.
docs.crmProductsDesc: Product catalog and the line items of each deal. While a deal has line items, its amount is the sum of their net totals (after discount, before tax) unless amountOverride is on.
docs.crmQuotesDesc: Quotes created from a deal's line items. Each quote keeps a snapshot of the items and has a public page (public_url) where the customer accepts or declines. Accepting fires the Flow event quote.accepted and the quote_accepted workflow trigger.
docs.crmAssociationsDesc: Many-to-many links between contacts, companies and deals. A contact or deal can have several companies; one of them is primary. contact.company_id always mirrors the primary company.
docs.crmTagsDesc: Workspace tags for contacts, companies and deals.
docs.productsListDesc: Products in the catalog, active first, sorted by name.
docs.productsCreateDesc: Adds a product to the catalog. Without currency it uses the workspace base currency.
docs.productsPatchDesc: Updates the fields you send. Line items already on deals don't change.
docs.productsDeleteDesc: Deletes the product. Line items that used it stay on their deals as custom items.
docs.lineItemsListDesc: Line items with their computed subtotal, discount, net, tax and total, plus the deal totals. Amounts are rounded per line to the deal currency.
docs.lineItemsCreateDesc: From a product (copies name, price, tax and recurrence; the price is converted to the deal currency when there is an exchange rate) or custom (name and unitPrice). Recalculates the deal amount.
docs.lineItemsPatchDesc: Updates quantity, price, discount, tax or text and recalculates the deal amount.
docs.lineItemsDeleteDesc: Removes the line item and recalculates the deal amount.
docs.quotesListDesc: Quotes of the workspace, newest first. Sent quotes past their expiration date are returned as expired.
docs.quotesCreateDesc: Creates a draft quote from the deal's current line items (the deal needs at least one). Defaults: expires in 30 days, recipient = first contact and primary company of the deal.
docs.quotesGetDesc: Returns the quote with its items and public_url.
docs.quotesPatchDesc: Edits a draft. status: "sent" publishes the public link (draft → sent). Accepting and declining happen on the public page. Non-draft quotes answer 409 not_draft.
docs.associationsListDesc: All records linked to a contact, company or deal. Companies also return their parent and child companies.
docs.associationsCreateDesc: Links contact ↔ company, deal ↔ company or deal ↔ contact (in either order). primary makes the company the primary one; label only applies to contact ↔ company. Linking an existing association updates its primary flag and label.
docs.associationsDeleteDesc: Unlinks two records (query parameters). Removing the primary company promotes the oldest remaining one.
docs.tagsListDesc: Tags with how many contacts, companies and deals use each one.
docs.tagsCreateDesc: Names are unique per workspace (case-insensitive). A duplicate answers 409 duplicate_tag.
docs.tagsPatchDesc: Renames the tag or changes its color.
docs.tagsDeleteDesc: Deletes the tag and removes it from every record.
docs.tagsRecordsDesc: Adds or removes the tag on up to 1000 records. Ids from other workspaces are ignored. Returns how many records changed.
docs.paramParentCompanyId: Parent company id (hierarchy). null makes it top-level. A company can't be its own ancestor.
docs.paramPrimaryCompanyId: Primary company id. It's associated if needed; the previous primary stays associated. null removes the primary.
docs.paramDealCompanyIds: Other companies to associate with the deal.
docs.paramAmountOverride: true keeps a manual amount even with line items; false recalculates it from the line items. Editing amount on a deal with line items turns it on.
docs.paramProductActiveFilter: true = active only, false = archived only.
docs.paramProductDescription: Description shown on line items and quotes.
docs.paramProductCurrency: ISO currency code (defaults to the workspace base currency).
docs.paramProductActive: false archives the product (hidden from pickers).
docs.paramRecurring: Billing interval: none, monthly or yearly.
docs.paramLineProductId: Catalog product id. Omit it for a custom line item.
docs.paramLineName: Line item name (required for custom items).
docs.paramUnitPrice: Unit price in the deal currency.
docs.paramQuoteDealId: Deal whose line items become the quote.
docs.paramQuoteTitle: Quote title (defaults to the deal name).
docs.paramQuoteSender: Sender details shown on the quote.
docs.paramQuoteRecipient: Recipient details (default: the deal's first contact and primary company).
docs.paramQuoteRefresh: Re-snapshot the deal's current line items (drafts only).
docs.paramAssocType: Record type: contact, company or deal.
docs.paramAssocPrimary: Make this the primary company of the contact or deal.
docs.paramAssocLabel: Contact ↔ company label: employee, decision_maker, billing, champion, influencer, former_employee (or empty).
docs.paramTagColor: Color: crm, link, cal, track, chat, docs, flow, agents, notes, board or robots.
docs.paramTagEntity: Record type: contact, company or deal.
docs.scopesIntro: Every key has scopes, chosen when you create it. Write scopes include read. Keys created before scopes existed have all of them. A request without the needed scope gets 403 insufficient_scope.
docs.scopesVisibility: A key acts as the person who created it: if your workspace limits members to their own (or their team’s) CRM records, the API returns only those records.
docs.scope_crm_read: Read contacts, companies, deals, activities, tasks, pipelines, products, quotes, tags, templates, sequences and forms.
docs.scope_crm_write: Create, update and delete CRM records, enroll in sequences, tag records (includes crm:read).
docs.scope_links_read: List links and read their stats.
docs.scope_links_write: Create, update and delete short links (includes links:read).
docs.scope_agents_run: Send messages to your AI agents.
docs.scope_robots_run: List and run robots, read their runs and batches.
docs.crmFormsDesc: Lead capture forms and their submissions. Each submission also creates or updates a contact and logs a "Form submitted" activity.
docs.formsListDesc: All forms in the workspace with their fields, status and submission count. `key` is the public slug (or token) used in /f/'<key>' and the embed script.
docs.formsSubmissionsDesc: Submissions of a form, newest first, with the submitted values, UTM parameters and the linked contact.
docs.paramLinkForwardParams: Pass the query string of the short link to the destination (default true). On a conflict the short link value wins; qr is never passed.
docs.paramLinkDoIndex: Allow search engines to index the short link (default false). Without it the redirect carries X-Robots-Tag: noindex.
docs.paramLinkExpiredUrl: Where the link redirects once it expires or reaches max_clicks. null clears it and the domain default or the zerosoft page is used.
docs.paramLinkUtm: Sets that utm_* parameter in the destination URL. An empty string or null removes it. The utm object of the link always mirrors the final URL.
docs.paramLinkDomain: Hostname of one of your verified custom domains. Leave it out to use the default domain.
docs.paramLinkExpiresAt: ISO 8601 date. After it, the link redirects to expiredUrl or shows the expired page.
docs.paramLinkMaxClicks: Clicks allowed before the link stops redirecting.
docs.paramLinkPassword: Visitors must type it before the redirect. It is stored hashed and never returned; the response only says has_password.
docs.paramLinkOg: Title, description and image (http(s) URL) for the preview in social networks and chat apps.
docs.paramLinkExternalId: Your own id for the link, unique per workspace (letters, digits and . _ : @ -). Read or update the link later with /api/v1/links/ext_{externalId}.
docs.paramLinkCreator: Only links created by this user id.
docs.paramMoveFields: Properties the stage requires, saved before moving: amount, closeDate, ownerId, priority, source, description and custom (custom field values by name).
docs.chatDesc: Read and answer the conversations of your Chat inbox from your own app or helpdesk. Needs the chat:read scope to read and chat:write to reply, assign and resolve. Replies are sent as the person who created the key.
docs.chatListDesc: Conversations of the workspace's widgets, most recently updated first.
docs.chatGetDesc: The conversation and all its messages, oldest first. Internal notes come with isNote: true.
docs.chatReplyDesc: Sends a message to the visitor (or an internal note with note: true). Like a reply from the inbox, it counts as the first response for the SLA and reopens the conversation if it was resolved. Fires chat.message.created.
docs.chatAssignDesc: Assigns the conversation to an agent of its widget, or unassigns it with null. Fires chat.conversation.assigned. Errors: 400 invalid_assignee.
docs.chatResolveDesc: Marks the conversation as resolved. If the widget has required attributes still empty, it answers 400 missing_attributes. Fires chat.conversation.resolved.
docs.chatReopenDesc: Opens a resolved or snoozed conversation again.
docs.paramChatAssignedTo: Only conversations assigned to this user id, or unassigned.
docs.paramChatLimit: How many to return (1 to 200, default 50).
docs.paramChatOffset: How many to skip, for paging.
docs.paramChatNote: true to leave an internal note the visitor doesn't see.
docs.paramChatAssignee: User id of the agent, or null to unassign.
docs.scope_chat_read: List Chat conversations and read their messages.
docs.scope_chat_write: Reply, assign, resolve and reopen Chat conversations (includes chat:read).
docs.webhooksChatDesc: Chat events carry the conversation. chat.message.created adds the message (visitor, teammate or bot; internal notes are not sent) and chat.conversation.assigned adds previousAssignedTo.
docs.groupsDesc: Read WhatsApp chats and groups, send messages and create tickets from your own systems. Messages go out from the number the chat belongs to.
docs.groupsChatsListDesc: Open chats and groups, most recent first, with labels, assignee and whether they wait for a reply.
docs.groupsMessagesListDesc: Messages and internal notes of a chat, oldest first.
docs.groupsMessagesSendDesc: Sends a WhatsApp message to the chat or group, or saves an internal note with note: true.
docs.groupsTicketsListDesc: Tickets created from WhatsApp messages, with SLA status.
docs.groupsTicketsCreateDesc: Creates a ticket on a chat. With messageId, a message has at most one ticket: repeating returns the existing one.
docs.paramGroupsFilter: all, unread, unanswered, flagged, mine, unassigned or closed
docs.paramGroupsAfter: Only messages after this ISO date
docs.paramGroupsNote: Save as an internal note instead of sending
docs.paramGroupsStatus: active (default), all, open, in_progress, resolved or closed
docs.paramGroupsTitle: Ticket title (default: the first line of the message)
docs.scope_groups_read: Read WhatsApp chats, messages and tickets in Groups.
docs.scope_groups_write: Send WhatsApp messages and create tickets in Groups.
